question.text: The Objectives Resolution was passed by the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan on
question.explanation: The Constituent Assembly adopted the Objectives Resolution on 12 March 1949, laying down the ideological basis of Pakistan's future constitutions.

question.text: The Objectives Resolution was moved in the Constituent Assembly by
question.explanation: Prime Minister Liaquat Ali Khan introduced the Objectives Resolution in the Constituent Assembly in March 1949.

question.text: According to the Objectives Resolution, sovereignty over the entire universe belongs to
question.explanation: The Resolution opens by declaring that sovereignty over the entire universe belongs to Allah Almighty alone, and authority is a sacred trust exercised by the people within His limits.

question.text: The Objectives Resolution was made a substantive part of the Constitution by
question.explanation: Until 1985 the Objectives Resolution was only a preamble; the Eighth Amendment inserted it into the operative text of the Constitution.

question.text: As a substantive part of the 1973 Constitution, the Objectives Resolution appears as
question.explanation: Article 2A gives the Objectives Resolution the status of a substantive provision of the Constitution.

question.text: From 1947 until the first Constitution was framed, Pakistan was governed under an adapted version of the
question.explanation: The Government of India Act 1935, as adapted under the Indian Independence Act 1947, served as Pakistan's interim constitution until 1956.

question.text: The first Constituent Assembly of Pakistan was dissolved in 1954 by Governor-General
question.explanation: Governor-General Ghulam Muhammad dissolved the first Constituent Assembly in October 1954, a step challenged in the Maulvi Tamizuddin Khan case.

question.text: The One Unit scheme, merging the provinces of West Pakistan into a single unit, was introduced in
question.explanation: The One Unit was established in 1955, combining the provinces and states of West Pakistan into one administrative unit.

question.text: The first Constitution of Pakistan came into force on
question.explanation: The 1956 Constitution was enforced on 23 March 1956, the anniversary of the Pakistan Resolution.

question.text: The Prime Minister of Pakistan when the 1956 Constitution was enforced was
question.explanation: Chaudhry Muhammad Ali headed the government that framed and enforced the 1956 Constitution.

question.text: The first President of Pakistan under the 1956 Constitution was
question.explanation: Iskander Mirza became the first President when the 1956 Constitution replaced the office of Governor-General.

question.text: The official title 'Islamic Republic of Pakistan' was adopted for the first time in the Constitution of
question.explanation: The 1956 Constitution formally named the country the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.

question.text: The 1956 Constitution of Pakistan was abrogated on
question.explanation: President Iskander Mirza abrogated the 1956 Constitution and imposed martial law on 7 October 1958.

question.text: The 1956 Constitution of Pakistan consisted of
question.explanation: Pakistan's first Constitution contained 234 articles arranged in thirteen parts with six schedules.

question.text: The Constitution Commission appointed in 1960 to recommend a new constitutional framework was headed by
question.explanation: Ayub Khan appointed a Constitution Commission in 1960 under Justice Muhammad Shahabuddin, whose report preceded the 1962 Constitution.

question.text: The second Constitution of Pakistan was promulgated on
question.explanation: The 1962 Constitution, framed under Ayub Khan, came into effect on 8 June 1962.

question.text: The form of government provided by the 1962 Constitution was
question.explanation: The 1962 Constitution concentrated executive authority in a directly responsible President, replacing the parliamentary system of 1956.

question.text: Under the 1962 Constitution the President was elected by an electoral college composed of
question.explanation: The elected members of the Basic Democracies system formed the electoral college for the presidency and the legislatures under the 1962 Constitution.

question.text: The 1962 Constitution was abrogated in 1969 by
question.explanation: General Yahya Khan abrogated the 1962 Constitution and imposed martial law in March 1969 after Ayub Khan handed over power.

question.text: The National Assembly passed the 1973 Constitution on
question.explanation: The Constitution Bill was approved by the National Assembly on 10 April 1973 and enforced later that year.

question.text: The 1973 Constitution of Pakistan came into force on
question.explanation: The 1973 Constitution became operative on 14 August 1973, when Zulfikar Ali Bhutto took office as Prime Minister.

question.text: The first Prime Minister under the 1973 Constitution was
question.explanation: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto assumed the office of Prime Minister when the 1973 Constitution took effect.

question.text: The first President under the 1973 Constitution was
question.explanation: Fazal Ilahi Chaudhry held the largely ceremonial presidency created by the 1973 Constitution.

question.text: The 1973 Constitution of Pakistan contains
question.explanation: The 1973 Constitution is arranged in twelve parts containing 280 articles.

question.text: A bicameral legislature at the centre was provided for the first time by the Constitution of
question.explanation: The 1973 Constitution created the Senate alongside the National Assembly; the 1956 and 1962 constitutions had single chambers.

question.text: Under Article 2 of the 1973 Constitution, the state religion of Pakistan is
question.explanation: Article 2 declares that Islam shall be the State religion of Pakistan.

question.text: Abrogating or subverting the Constitution amounts to high treason under
question.explanation: Article 6 declares any act of abrogating, subverting or suspending the Constitution by force to be high treason.

question.text: Fundamental Rights in the 1973 Constitution are contained in Articles
question.explanation: Part II Chapter 1 of the Constitution sets out Fundamental Rights in Articles 8 to 28.

question.text: The right to a fair trial and due process was inserted into the Constitution as
question.explanation: Article 10A, added by the Eighteenth Amendment in 2010, guarantees the right to a fair trial and due process.

question.text: Freedom of association and the right to form political parties are guaranteed by
question.explanation: Article 17 protects freedom of association, including the right of citizens to form or be members of political parties.

question.text: Freedom of speech and expression is guaranteed by which article of the 1973 Constitution?
question.explanation: Article 19 guarantees freedom of speech and expression subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by law.

question.text: The right to information in matters of public importance is provided by
question.explanation: Article 19A, inserted by the Eighteenth Amendment, gives every citizen the right to have access to information in all matters of public importance.

question.text: Equality of all citizens before law is guaranteed by
question.explanation: Article 25 declares all citizens equal before law and entitled to equal protection of law.

question.text: Free and compulsory education for children aged five to sixteen years is guaranteed by
question.explanation: Article 25A, added by the Eighteenth Amendment, obliges the State to provide free and compulsory education to children aged five to sixteen.

question.text: Which article requires all existing laws to be brought into conformity with the injunctions of Islam as laid down in the Quran and Sunnah?
question.explanation: Article 227 requires existing laws to conform to Islamic injunctions and bars enactment of any law repugnant to them.

question.text: The Council of Islamic Ideology is constituted under which article of the 1973 Constitution?
question.explanation: Article 228 provides for the constitution of the Council of Islamic Ideology and the appointment of its members.

question.text: Under Article 251 of the Constitution, the national language of Pakistan is
question.explanation: Article 251 declares Urdu the national language and required arrangements for its use for official purposes within fifteen years of the commencing day.

question.text: Defection by a member of Parliament from his political party is dealt with under
question.explanation: Article 63A allows the party head to declare a defecting member for disqualification, with the matter decided by the Election Commission and appealable to the Supreme Court.

question.text: A bill to amend the Constitution must be passed by the votes of not less than
options: Two-thirds of the total membership of each House
Three-fourths of the total membership of each House
Two-thirds of a joint sitting only
A simple majority of members present in each House
question.explanation: Article 239 requires a constitutional amendment bill to be passed by two-thirds of the total membership of each House of Parliament.

question.text: The minimum age prescribed for a person to be elected President of Pakistan is
question.explanation: Article 41 requires the President to be a Muslim of not less than forty-five years of age who is qualified to be elected a member of the National Assembly.

question.text: The term of office of the President of Pakistan is
question.explanation: Article 44 fixes the President's term at five years from the day he enters upon office.

question.text: The President of Pakistan is elected by an electoral college consisting of
options: Members of the National Assembly only
Members of both Houses of Parliament only
Members of both Houses of Parliament and the Provincial Assemblies
question.explanation: Article 41 provides that the President is elected by members of the Senate, the National Assembly and the four Provincial Assemblies.

question.text: The President may be removed through impeachment by a resolution passed by
options: A simple majority of a joint sitting
Two-thirds of the total membership of Parliament in a joint sitting
question.explanation: Article 47 requires not less than two-thirds of the total membership of Parliament, voting in a joint sitting, to remove or impeach the President.

question.text: Under Article 48 of the Constitution, the President shall generally act
options: On and in accordance with the advice of the Cabinet or the Prime Minister
On the advice of the Chief Justice
On the advice of the Chairman of the Senate
question.explanation: Article 48 binds the President to act on the advice of the Cabinet or the Prime Minister, except where the Constitution allows him to act in his discretion.

question.text: An Ordinance promulgated by the President remains in force for
question.explanation: Under Article 89 an Ordinance stands repealed after 120 days unless extended once for a further 120 days by a resolution of the National Assembly.

question.text: If the office of President becomes vacant, his functions are performed by the
question.explanation: Article 49 provides that the Chairman of the Senate, or in his absence the Speaker of the National Assembly, acts as President until a new President is elected.

question.text: The total number of seats in the National Assembly of Pakistan after the Twenty-fifth Amendment is
question.explanation: The merger of FATA into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa reduced the National Assembly from 342 to 336 seats.

question.text: The number of seats reserved for women in the National Assembly is
question.explanation: Article 51 reserves sixty seats in the National Assembly for women, filled through proportional representation from party lists.

question.text: The number of seats reserved for non-Muslims in the National Assembly is
question.explanation: Ten National Assembly seats are reserved for non-Muslims under Article 51.

question.text: The total membership of the Senate of Pakistan after the Twenty-fifth Amendment is
question.explanation: The Twenty-fifth Amendment abolished the four Senate seats of FATA and reduced the House from 104 to 96 members.

question.text: The term of office of a member of the Senate of Pakistan is
question.explanation: Senators are elected for six years, with half the House retiring every three years.

question.text: Each province is represented in the Senate of Pakistan by
question.explanation: Each Provincial Assembly elects 23 senators, comprising 14 general, 4 women, 4 technocrats or ulema and 1 non-Muslim member.

question.text: The normal term of the National Assembly of Pakistan is
question.explanation: Article 52 fixes the National Assembly's term at five years from the day of its first sitting unless dissolved earlier.

question.text: The minimum age for election as a member of the National Assembly is
question.explanation: Article 62 requires a candidate for the National Assembly to be not less than twenty-five years of age.

question.text: The minimum voting age for elections to the National Assembly of Pakistan is
question.explanation: Citizens of Pakistan who are not less than eighteen years of age and enrolled on the electoral roll may vote.

question.text: Under the 1973 Constitution a money bill may originate only in the
question.explanation: Article 73 provides that a money bill originates in the National Assembly; the Senate may only make recommendations on it.

question.text: Under the 1973 Constitution, the office of Prime Minister of Pakistan can be held only by
options: A person of at least forty-five years of age
question.explanation: Article 91 requires that the Prime Minister be a Muslim, as does Article 41 for the President.

question.text: A vote of no-confidence against the Prime Minister is provided for in
question.explanation: Article 95 lays down the procedure for a resolution of no-confidence against the Prime Minister in the National Assembly.

question.text: The Prime Minister of Pakistan is elected by
options: A majority of the total membership of the National Assembly
A majority of the members present in the National Assembly
question.explanation: Article 91 requires the Prime Minister to secure the votes of a majority of the total membership of the National Assembly.

question.text: Under the Eighteenth Amendment, the total strength of the federal Cabinet including Ministers of State may not exceed
options: 15 per cent of the total membership of Parliament
20 per cent of the National Assembly
11 per cent of the total membership of Parliament
question.explanation: Article 92 caps the federal Cabinet, including Ministers of State, at eleven per cent of the total membership of Parliament.

question.text: A Proclamation of Emergency on account of war, external aggression or internal disturbance is issued under
question.explanation: Article 232 empowers the President to proclaim an emergency when the security of Pakistan is threatened by war, external aggression or internal disturbance beyond a province's control.

question.text: Command and control of the Armed Forces of Pakistan is dealt with in which article of the Constitution?
question.explanation: Article 243 vests control and command of the Armed Forces in the Federal Government and provides for the appointment of the services chiefs.

question.text: The writ jurisdiction of a High Court is derived from which article of the Constitution?
question.explanation: Article 199 empowers a High Court to issue writs for the enforcement of rights within its territorial jurisdiction.

question.text: The original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court in questions of public importance concerning fundamental rights arises under
question.explanation: Article 184(3) allows the Supreme Court to act where a question of public importance relating to the enforcement of fundamental rights is involved.

question.text: The advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court, exercised on a reference by the President, is contained in
question.explanation: Article 186 allows the President to refer a question of law of public importance to the Supreme Court for its opinion.

question.text: A judge of the Supreme Court of Pakistan retires at the age of
question.explanation: Article 179 fixes the retirement age of a Supreme Court judge at sixty-five years.

question.text: The Supreme Judicial Council of Pakistan is provided for in
question.explanation: Article 209 establishes the Supreme Judicial Council to inquire into the capacity or conduct of judges of the superior courts.

question.text: The Supreme Judicial Council consists of the Chief Justice of Pakistan,
options: The Chief Justices of all High Courts
Two next most senior Supreme Court judges and two most senior High Court Chief Justices
The Attorney General and the Federal Law Minister
Four judges nominated by the President
question.explanation: Article 209 composes the Council of the Chief Justice of Pakistan, the two next most senior judges of the Supreme Court and the two most senior Chief Justices of the High Courts.

question.text: The Federal Shariat Court of Pakistan was established in
question.explanation: The Federal Shariat Court was created in 1980 to examine whether laws are repugnant to the injunctions of Islam.

question.text: The Judicial Commission of Pakistan for the appointment of superior court judges was created by inserting
question.explanation: Article 175A, inserted by the Eighteenth Amendment, established the Judicial Commission and the Parliamentary Committee for judicial appointments.

question.text: The permanent seat of the Supreme Court of Pakistan is at
question.explanation: The Constitution places the seat of the Supreme Court at Islamabad, with registries in the provincial capitals.

question.text: The Council of Common Interests is constituted under which article of the 1973 Constitution?
question.explanation: Article 153 provides for the constitution of the Council of Common Interests by the President.

question.text: The Council of Common Interests is chaired by the
question.explanation: Since the Eighteenth Amendment the Prime Minister is the chairman of the Council of Common Interests.

question.text: The Council of Common Interests consists of how many members in total?
question.explanation: The Council has eight members: the Prime Minister as chairman, the four Chief Ministers and three members of the Federal Government nominated by the Prime Minister.

question.text: The Constitution requires the Council of Common Interests to meet at least once in every
question.explanation: Article 154 obliges the Council of Common Interests to meet at least once in ninety days.

question.text: Under the Constitution the Council of Common Interests is responsible to
question.explanation: Article 154 makes the Council of Common Interests responsible to Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament), to which it submits an annual report.

question.text: A complaint by a province about interference with its water supplies is referred under Article 155 to the
question.explanation: Article 155 provides that such a complaint is made to the Council of Common Interests, which may appoint a commission to investigate it.

question.text: The National Economic Council under Article 156 of the Constitution is headed by the
question.explanation: Since the Eighteenth Amendment the Prime Minister chairs the National Economic Council, which reviews the overall economic condition of the country.

question.text: Under Article 160 the National Finance Commission must be constituted at intervals not exceeding
question.explanation: Article 160 requires the President to constitute a National Finance Commission at intervals not exceeding five years.

question.text: The National Finance Commission is chaired by the
options: Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan
question.explanation: The Federal Minister for Finance heads the National Finance Commission, whose other members include the provincial finance ministers.

question.text: Under the Seventh National Finance Commission Award the provincial share in the divisible pool was raised to
question.explanation: The Seventh NFC Award increased the provinces' share of the divisible pool to 57.5 per cent from the second year of the award.

question.text: In the Seventh NFC Award the weight assigned to population in the horizontal distribution among provinces was
question.explanation: The Seventh NFC Award used multiple criteria for the first time, giving population 82 per cent weight alongside poverty, revenue generation and inverse population density.

question.text: The Eighteenth Amendment added a clause to Article 160 providing that a province's share in each NFC award shall not be
options: Less than its share in the previous award
question.explanation: Article 160(3A) guarantees that the share of the provinces in each successive award shall not be less than that given in the previous award.

question.text: Under Article 161 the net proceeds of the excise duty on natural gas and the royalty on crude oil are paid to
options: The province in which the well-head is situated
question.explanation: Article 161 assigns these proceeds to the province in which the well-head of natural gas or crude oil is located.

question.text: Under Article 172(3), inserted by the Eighteenth Amendment, mineral oil and natural gas within a province vest
options: Jointly and equally in the province and the Federal Government
In the Council of Common Interests
question.explanation: Article 172(3) gives the province concerned and the Federal Government joint and equal ownership of mineral oil and natural gas within the province.

question.text: The Chief Election Commissioner of Pakistan is appointed by the
question.explanation: Article 213 provides that the Chief Election Commissioner is appointed by the President following the consultation procedure laid down in the Constitution.

question.text: The Election Commission of Pakistan consists of the Chief Election Commissioner and
question.explanation: Article 218 composes the Commission of the Chief Election Commissioner as chairman and four members, one from each province.

question.text: The term of office of the Chief Election Commissioner of Pakistan is
question.explanation: The Eighteenth Amendment fixed the Chief Election Commissioner's term at five years.

question.text: A general election must be held within how many days of the expiry of the National Assembly's term?
question.explanation: Article 224 requires a general election within sixty days of the natural expiry of the Assembly's term.

question.text: Detailed constitutional provisions for the appointment of caretaker governments were introduced by the
question.explanation: The Twentieth Amendment of 2012 laid down the procedure for appointing caretaker Prime Ministers and Chief Ministers in consultation with the opposition.

question.text: Under Article 226 of the Constitution all elections are held by secret ballot except the election of the
question.explanation: Article 226 exempts the elections of the Prime Minister and the Chief Ministers from the requirement of a secret ballot.

question.text: Which article of the Constitution obliges each province to establish a local government system and devolve authority to elected local representatives?
question.explanation: Article 140A requires every province to establish a local government system and devolve political, administrative and financial responsibility to elected representatives.

question.text: Under the Eighteenth Amendment, elections to local governments in Pakistan are to be held by the
question.explanation: Clause (2) of Article 140A, added in 2010, assigns the conduct of local government elections to the Election Commission of Pakistan.

question.text: The Governor of a province is appointed by the
question.explanation: Article 101 provides that the President appoints the Governor of a province on the advice of the Prime Minister.

question.text: A Chief Minister of a province is elected by
options: A majority of members present in the Provincial Assembly
The Prime Minister on the Governor's advice
A majority of the total membership of the Provincial Assembly
question.explanation: Article 130 requires the Chief Minister to be elected by the votes of a majority of the total membership of the Provincial Assembly.

question.text: Where a provincial law is inconsistent with an Act of Parliament that Parliament is competent to enact, the Constitution provides that
options: The matter goes to the Council of Common Interests
question.explanation: Article 143 provides that the Act of Parliament prevails and the inconsistent provincial law is void to the extent of the inconsistency.

question.text: The Auditor-General of Pakistan is appointed by the
question.explanation: Article 168 provides for the appointment of the Auditor-General of Pakistan by the President.

question.text: The power of the President to dissolve the National Assembly in his discretion under Article 58(2)(b) was introduced by the
question.explanation: The Eighth Amendment of 1985 inserted Article 58(2)(b), giving the President discretionary power to dissolve the National Assembly.

question.text: Article 58(2)(b) was deleted from the Constitution in 1997 by the
question.explanation: The Thirteenth Amendment, passed in 1997, stripped the President of the discretionary power to dissolve the National Assembly.

question.text: The Fourteenth Amendment of 1997 was primarily concerned with
options: Disqualification of members on defection from their party
question.explanation: The Fourteenth Amendment introduced anti-defection provisions to prevent floor crossing by legislators.

question.text: The Seventeenth Amendment, passed in 2003, is best known for
options: Restoring the President's power to dissolve the National Assembly
Creating the Council of Common Interests
question.explanation: The Seventeenth Amendment revived Article 58(2)(b) and validated the Legal Framework Order issued during General Musharraf's rule.

question.text: The Eighteenth Amendment to the Constitution of Pakistan was passed in
question.explanation: The Eighteenth Amendment was approved by Parliament and assented to in April 2010.

question.text: The Concurrent Legislative List was abolished by the
question.explanation: The Eighteenth Amendment deleted the Concurrent Legislative List, transferring its subjects to the provinces.

question.text: The North-West Frontier Province was renamed Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by the
question.explanation: The Eighteenth Amendment of 2010 changed the name of the North-West Frontier Province to Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

question.text: The parliamentary committee that drafted the Eighteenth Amendment was chaired by
question.explanation: Senator Mian Raza Rabbani headed the Parliamentary Committee on Constitutional Reforms that produced the Eighteenth Amendment.

question.text: The Twenty-first Amendment to the Constitution was passed to
options: Establish military courts for terrorism cases
Create the office of caretaker Prime Minister
Fix the tenure of the Chief Justice
question.explanation: Passed in January 2015 after the Peshawar school attack, the Twenty-first Amendment allowed military courts to try terrorism suspects.

question.text: The Twenty-first Amendment contained a sunset clause under which it was to expire after
question.explanation: The military courts created by the Twenty-first Amendment were given a life of two years from the date of commencement.

question.text: The Twenty-fifth Amendment to the Constitution of Pakistan provided for the
options: Creation of the Council of Common Interests
Merger of FATA with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
question.explanation: The Twenty-fifth Amendment of 2018 merged the Federally Administered Tribal Areas into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and omitted Article 247.

question.text: The Second Amendment to the 1973 Constitution, passed in 1974, dealt with
question.explanation: The Second Amendment amended Article 260 to define who is a Muslim, declaring Ahmadis to be non-Muslims for constitutional purposes.

question.text: The Twenty-sixth Amendment of 2024 fixed the tenure of the Chief Justice of Pakistan at
question.explanation: The Twenty-sixth Amendment limited the Chief Justice of Pakistan to a three-year term and provided for constitutional benches in the Supreme Court.

question.text: In which year did Sir Syed Ahmad Khan die?
question.explanation: Sir Syed died on 27 March 1898 at Aligarh and was buried beside the mosque of the college he had founded.

question.text: The Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College at Aligarh was established in which year?
question.explanation: Sir Syed opened the school at Aligarh in 1875, which was raised to the status of a college in 1877.

question.text: Which book did Sir Syed Ahmad Khan write to explain the causes of the 1857 uprising?
question.explanation: In Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind Sir Syed argued that British ignorance of Indian feeling, not Muslim disloyalty, had caused the revolt.

question.text: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan launched the magazine Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq in which year?
question.explanation: Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq was started in 1870 to promote social and intellectual reform among Indian Muslims.

question.text: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded the Scientific Society in 1864 at which place?
question.explanation: The Scientific Society was established at Ghazipur in 1864 to translate Western works on science into Urdu, and was later moved to Aligarh.

question.text: The Urdu-Hindi controversy of 1867, which deepened Sir Syed's belief in Muslim separateness, began in which city?
question.explanation: A movement at Banaras in 1867 demanded that Hindi in Devanagari script replace Urdu in the courts, convincing Sir Syed that Hindus and Muslims could not remain one nation.

question.text: The Muhammadan Educational Conference was founded by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan in which year?
question.explanation: Founded in 1886, the Muhammadan Educational Conference met annually across India to spread modern education among Muslims and later provided the platform on which the Muslim League was formed.

question.text: Which Viceroy ordered the partition of Bengal in 1905?
question.explanation: Lord Curzon carried out the partition of Bengal on administrative grounds, dividing a province that was too large to govern effectively.

question.text: The partition of Bengal took effect on 16 October of which year?
question.explanation: The partition became effective on 16 October 1905, a day observed by Hindu opponents as a day of mourning.

question.text: What was the capital of the new province of Eastern Bengal and Assam created in 1905?
question.explanation: Dacca became the capital of Eastern Bengal and Assam, giving the Muslim-majority east its own administrative centre.

question.text: In which year was the partition of Bengal annulled?
question.explanation: The partition was reversed in 1911 in the face of sustained Hindu agitation, which convinced Muslims that British assurances were unreliable.

question.text: Which Muslim leader of Dacca was the strongest supporter of the partition of Bengal?
question.explanation: Nawab Salimullah Khan of Dacca championed the partition because it gave the Muslims of eastern Bengal an administration of their own.

question.text: The Simla Deputation waited upon the Viceroy on 1 October of which year?
question.explanation: The deputation of Muslim notables met the Viceroy at Simla on 1 October 1906, three months before the Muslim League was founded.

question.text: Who led the Simla Deputation of 1906?
question.explanation: Sir Aga Khan III headed the deputation and read the address presented to the Viceroy.

question.text: How many members made up the Simla Deputation of 1906?
question.explanation: Thirty-five Muslim leaders drawn from all provinces of India formed the deputation that met Lord Minto.

question.text: The central demand of the Simla Deputation was for
options: Urdu as the official language of India
the abolition of the zamindari system
question.explanation: The deputation asked that Muslims be given separate electorates and weightage in representation because of their political importance, a demand conceded in 1909.

question.text: The All India Muslim League was founded on 30 December of which year?
question.explanation: The League was founded on 30 December 1906 during the annual session of the Muhammadan Educational Conference.

question.text: In which city was the All India Muslim League founded?
question.explanation: The League was founded at Dacca, where the Muhammadan Educational Conference was holding its annual session.

question.text: Who was the first President of the All India Muslim League?
question.explanation: Sir Aga Khan III was chosen as the first President of the League and held the office until 1912.

question.text: The London branch of the All India Muslim League was established in 1908 by
question.explanation: Syed Ameer Ali set up the League's London branch in 1908 to present the Muslim case before British opinion.

question.text: Muhammad Ali Jinnah formally joined the All India Muslim League in which year?
question.explanation: Jinnah joined the League in 1913 after it adopted self-government as its aim, while retaining his Congress membership for some years.

question.text: Muhammad Ali Jinnah was born on 25 December of which year?
question.explanation: Jinnah was born at Karachi on 25 December 1876.

question.text: Jinnah was first elected to the Imperial Legislative Council in 1910 as a Muslim member from
question.explanation: Jinnah entered the Imperial Legislative Council in 1910 as the Muslim member for Bombay.

question.text: Which measure did Jinnah pilot through the Imperial Legislative Council in 1913 to protect Muslim family endowments?
question.explanation: Jinnah secured passage of the Mussalman Wakf Validating Act, commonly called the Wakf Alal Aulad Act, restoring the legality of family endowments.

question.text: The Lucknow Pact was concluded in which year?
question.explanation: The Congress and the Muslim League concluded the Lucknow Pact in December 1916 on a joint scheme of constitutional reform.

question.text: Under the Lucknow Pact the Indian National Congress for the first time accepted
question.explanation: The chief Muslim gain from the Lucknow Pact was Congress recognition of separate electorates and of weightage for Muslims in minority provinces.

question.text: Who gave Jinnah the title 'Ambassador of Hindu-Muslim Unity'?
question.explanation: Sarojini Naidu described Jinnah as the Ambassador of Hindu-Muslim Unity for his role in bringing about the Lucknow Pact.

question.text: Who ordered the firing at Jallianwala Bagh?
question.explanation: Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer commanded the troops that fired on the crowd at Jallianwala Bagh.

question.text: The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms of 1919 introduced which system in the provinces?
question.explanation: The Government of India Act 1919 introduced dyarchy, dividing provincial subjects into reserved and transferred halves.

question.text: The Khilafat Movement was launched in which year?
question.explanation: The Khilafat Movement began in 1919 to defend the Ottoman Caliphate after the Turkish defeat in the First World War.

question.text: The All India Khilafat Committee was formed in 1919 in which city?
question.explanation: The All India Khilafat Committee was set up at Bombay in 1919 to organise the movement and raise funds for it.

question.text: The 'Ali Brothers' of the Khilafat Movement were
options: Zafar Ali Khan and Shaukat Ali
Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Zafar Ali Khan
Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Shaukat Ali
Shaukat Ali and Syed Ameer Ali
question.explanation: Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Maulana Shaukat Ali led the Khilafat agitation and were known as the Ali Brothers.

question.text: The Hijrat Movement of 1920 involved the migration of Indian Muslims to
question.explanation: Thousands of Muslims left for Afghanistan in 1920 after India was declared dar-ul-harb, but the migration ended in hardship and failure.

question.text: The newspaper 'Al-Hilal' was launched in 1912 by
question.explanation: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad brought out Al-Hilal from Calcutta in 1912, giving Urdu journalism a militant anti-British tone.

question.text: The Simon Commission was appointed by the British government in which year?
question.explanation: The commission was appointed in 1927 to review the working of the 1919 reforms and reached India in 1928.

question.text: Indian parties boycotted the Simon Commission chiefly because
options: it recommended the partition of India
it proposed to abolish separate electorates
it was headed by a serving general
question.explanation: All seven members of the commission were British, which Indians of every party resented as a denial of their fitness to shape their own constitution.

question.text: The committee that produced the Nehru Report of 1928 was chaired by
question.explanation: Motilal Nehru chaired the committee appointed by the All Parties Conference to draft a constitution for India.

question.text: On the question of representation, the Nehru Report recommended
options: reservation of half the seats for Muslims
question.explanation: The report proposed joint electorates with reservation in some cases, which Muslims saw as the withdrawal of the safeguard granted in 1909 and confirmed in 1916.

question.text: Jinnah presented his Fourteen Points in which year?
question.explanation: Jinnah placed the Fourteen Points before the Muslim League in March 1929 as the Muslim answer to the Nehru Report.

question.text: One of Jinnah's Fourteen Points demanded that Muslim representation in the central legislature should not be less than
question.explanation: The points required that Muslims be given not less than one-third of the seats in the central legislature.

question.text: The Delhi Muslim Proposals were put forward by Jinnah in which year?
question.explanation: In 1927 Jinnah offered to give up separate electorates in return for stated safeguards, an offer set aside after the Nehru Report.

question.text: Allama Iqbal delivered his famous Allahabad Address in which year?
question.explanation: Iqbal delivered the address in December 1930, outlining the idea of a consolidated Muslim state in north-western India.

question.text: In the Allahabad Address Iqbal proposed the amalgamation of which areas into a single state?
options: Punjab, North-West Frontier Province, Sindh and Balochistan
question.explanation: Iqbal called for the Punjab, the North-West Frontier Province, Sindh and Balochistan to be amalgamated into a single state.

question.text: Allama Iqbal died on
question.explanation: Iqbal died at Lahore on 21 April 1938, nine years before the state he had envisaged came into being.

question.text: Allama Iqbal obtained his doctorate from a university in which city?
question.explanation: Iqbal took his doctorate from the University of Munich in 1908 with a thesis on the development of metaphysics in Persia.

question.text: Allama Iqbal was knighted in which year?
question.explanation: Iqbal received a knighthood in 1922 in recognition of his poetry and scholarship.

question.text: Which party boycotted the First Round Table Conference of 1930-31?
question.explanation: The Congress stayed away from the First Round Table Conference because its leaders were in jail during the civil disobedience movement.

question.text: Gandhi personally attended which Round Table Conference?
question.explanation: Gandhi attended only the Second Round Table Conference of 1931 as the sole representative of the Congress.

question.text: Gandhi's participation in the Second Round Table Conference followed which agreement?
question.explanation: Under the Gandhi-Irwin Pact of March 1931 civil disobedience was suspended and the Congress agreed to attend the conference.

question.text: The Third Round Table Conference was held in which year?
question.explanation: The third and last conference met in London late in 1932 and was attended by only a small number of delegates.

question.text: The Communal Award of 1932 was announced by the British Prime Minister
question.explanation: Ramsay MacDonald announced the Communal Award in August 1932 after the Round Table Conferences failed to reach a communal settlement.

question.text: The name 'Pakistan' was coined by
question.explanation: Chaudhry Rahmat Ali coined the name in 1933 in a pamphlet issued from Cambridge.

question.text: Chaudhry Rahmat Ali's pamphlet of 1933 in which the name Pakistan first appeared was titled
question.explanation: The pamphlet Now or Never, issued on 28 January 1933, first used the word Pakistan for the Muslim homeland in north-western India.

question.text: The Government of India Act 1935 introduced which system in the provinces?
options: Nomination of ministers by the Viceroy
question.explanation: The Act of 1935 abolished provincial dyarchy and gave the provinces autonomy under ministers responsible to elected legislatures.

question.text: Under the constitutional changes of the mid-1930s, Sindh was made a separate province by separating it from
question.explanation: Sindh, long a part of the Bombay Presidency, became a separate province in 1936 under the Government of India Act 1935.

question.text: The Muslim League observed the 'Day of Deliverance' on 22 December of which year?
question.explanation: Jinnah called for a Day of Deliverance on 22 December 1939 after the Congress ministries resigned.

question.text: The Pirpur Report of 1938 dealt with
options: Muslim grievances under the Congress ministries
the demarcation of the Punjab boundary
question.explanation: The committee headed by Raja Syed Muhammad Mehdi of Pirpur inquired into Muslim complaints against the Congress provincial governments.

question.text: The Sikandar-Jinnah Pact was concluded in which year?
question.explanation: Sir Sikandar Hayat Khan agreed in 1937 that Muslim members of his Unionist Party would join the Muslim League, greatly strengthening it in the Punjab.

question.text: A. K. Fazlul Haq was popularly known as
question.explanation: Fazlul Haq, Premier of Bengal, was called Sher-e-Bengal, the Lion of Bengal.

question.text: Jinnah returned permanently from England to India to reorganise the Muslim League in
question.explanation: Jinnah gave up his London practice and returned in 1934, when he was elected permanent president of the Muslim League.

question.text: Liaquat Ali Khan became Honorary General Secretary of the All India Muslim League in
question.explanation: Liaquat Ali Khan was elected general secretary in 1936 and held the office until independence.

question.text: The Lahore Resolution was passed on
question.explanation: The resolution was adopted on 23 March 1940 on the concluding day of the League's Lahore session.

question.text: The Lahore Resolution of 1940 was moved by
question.explanation: A. K. Fazlul Haq, then Premier of Bengal, moved the resolution before the Lahore session.

question.text: The Lahore session of the Muslim League in March 1940 was presided over by
question.explanation: Jinnah presided over the Lahore session and in his address set out the case that Muslims were a nation by every definition.

question.text: The Lahore Resolution was passed at which ground in Lahore?
question.explanation: The session was held at Minto Park, now Iqbal Park, where the Minar-e-Pakistan later marked the spot.

question.text: The Delhi Convention of Muslim League legislators in April 1946 amended the Lahore Resolution to demand
options: dominion status within the British Empire
a federation with India at the centre
a single independent state of Pakistan
question.explanation: The 1946 convention replaced the wording about independent states with the demand for one sovereign state of Pakistan comprising the Muslim-majority zones.

question.text: Which was the first provincial legislature in British India to pass a resolution in favour of Pakistan?
question.explanation: The Sindh Legislative Assembly was the first to adopt a resolution supporting the demand for Pakistan.

question.text: The Cripps Mission came to India in which year?
question.explanation: Sir Stafford Cripps arrived in March 1942 with proposals meant to secure Indian support for the war effort.

question.text: Who described the Cripps proposals as 'a post-dated cheque'?
question.explanation: Gandhi dismissed the offer of dominion status after the war as a post-dated cheque, because nothing was to be conceded immediately.

question.text: The Quit India Movement was launched in August of which year?
question.explanation: The Congress passed the Quit India resolution in August 1942, after which its leadership was imprisoned for the rest of the war.

question.text: The C. R. Formula of 1944 was an attempt to settle the deadlock between
options: the British government and the Congress
the Congress and the princely states
the Muslim League and the Sikhs
the Congress and the Muslim League
question.explanation: C. Rajagopalachari's formula offered a plebiscite in the Muslim-majority districts in return for League cooperation, and formed the basis of the Gandhi-Jinnah talks.

question.text: The Gandhi-Jinnah talks of September 1944 were held in which city?
question.explanation: Gandhi met Jinnah at Jinnah's Bombay residence in September 1944, but the talks broke down over the definition of Pakistan.

question.text: The Simla Conference of 1945 was convened by which Viceroy?
question.explanation: Lord Wavell called the Simla Conference in June 1945 to form a new Executive Council of Indian members.

question.text: The Simla Conference of 1945 failed mainly because of a disagreement over
options: the Muslim League's claim to nominate all Muslim members of the Executive Council
the date of British withdrawal from India
the future of the princely states
question.explanation: Jinnah insisted that the League alone could nominate the Muslim members, a claim the Congress refused to accept, and the conference collapsed.

question.text: In the elections to the Central Legislative Assembly held in 1945-46, the Muslim League won
options: twenty of the thirty Muslim seats
twenty-five of the thirty Muslim seats
question.explanation: The League captured every one of the thirty Muslim seats in the central assembly, establishing its claim to speak for Indian Muslims.

question.text: Who was the Viceroy of India when the Lahore Resolution was passed?
question.explanation: Lord Linlithgow was Viceroy from 1936 to 1943 and therefore held office in March 1940.

question.text: The Cabinet Mission reached India in which month and year?
question.explanation: The three British ministers arrived in India in March 1946 to negotiate the transfer of power.

question.text: The Cabinet Mission of 1946 was headed by
question.explanation: Lord Pethick-Lawrence, the Secretary of State for India, led the mission as its senior member.

question.text: The Cabinet Mission Plan was announced on
question.explanation: The mission published its own plan on 16 May 1946 after the Simla talks between the Congress and the League failed.

question.text: Into how many groups or sections did the Cabinet Mission Plan divide the provinces of British India?
question.explanation: The plan placed the provinces in three sections, labelled A, B and C, within a loose federation.

question.text: Under the Cabinet Mission Plan, Group B was to consist of
options: Bombay, Madras and the United Provinces
the Punjab, the North-West Frontier Province and Sindh
question.explanation: Group B comprised the Muslim-majority provinces of the north-west, while Group C contained Bengal and Assam.

question.text: The Muslim League observed Direct Action Day on
question.explanation: Direct Action Day was observed on 16 August 1946 and was followed by severe rioting in Calcutta.

question.text: The Muslim League called Direct Action Day after withdrawing its acceptance of
question.explanation: The League withdrew its acceptance of the Cabinet Mission Plan when the Congress placed its own interpretation on the grouping clauses.

question.text: The Interim Government took office on 2 September of which year?
question.explanation: The Interim Government headed by Jawaharlal Nehru was sworn in on 2 September 1946, and the Muslim League joined it in October.

question.text: Which portfolio did Liaquat Ali Khan hold in the Interim Government of 1946?
question.explanation: Liaquat Ali Khan took charge of Finance and used the department to demonstrate the League's weight within the Interim Government.

question.text: Prime Minister Attlee announced Britain's intention to transfer power in India by June 1948 on
question.explanation: Attlee's statement of 20 February 1947 fixed a deadline for withdrawal and announced the appointment of a new Viceroy.

question.text: Who was the last Viceroy of British India?
question.explanation: Lord Mountbatten succeeded Lord Wavell in March 1947 and presided over the transfer of power.

question.text: The plan for the partition of India announced on 3 June 1947 is also known as the
question.explanation: The 3 June Plan, drawn up under Lord Mountbatten, provided the scheme by which British India was divided.

question.text: Under the 3 June Plan a referendum was to be held in the North-West Frontier Province and in
question.explanation: Referendums were prescribed for the North-West Frontier Province and for the Sylhet district of Assam.

question.text: The referendum in the North-West Frontier Province was held in which month of 1947?
question.explanation: The referendum took place in July 1947 and returned a large majority in favour of joining Pakistan, though the Khudai Khidmatgars boycotted it.

question.text: The 1947 referendum in Sylhet resulted in the district joining
question.explanation: Sylhet voted to leave Assam and join East Bengal, and so became part of Pakistan.

question.text: The decision of British Balochistan to join Pakistan in 1947 was taken by
question.explanation: The Shahi Jirga of Quetta, together with the non-official members of the Quetta municipality, voted in June 1947 for accession to Pakistan.

question.text: The Indian Independence Act received the royal assent on
question.explanation: The British Parliament passed the Indian Independence Act, which received the royal assent on 18 July 1947.

question.text: Who was appointed chairman of the Punjab and Bengal Boundary Commissions?
question.explanation: Sir Cyril Radcliffe chaired both boundary commissions, and the resulting line bears his name.

question.text: The Radcliffe Award was made public on
question.explanation: The boundary award was published on 17 August 1947, three days after Pakistan came into being.

question.text: Apart from its chairman, each Boundary Commission of 1947 consisted of how many members?
question.explanation: Each commission had four members, two nominated by the Congress and two by the Muslim League, so the chairman's casting voice decided every disputed point.

question.text: Which Muslim-majority district was controversially awarded to India by the Radcliffe Award?
question.explanation: Most of Gurdaspur district went to India despite its Muslim majority, giving India a land route to Kashmir.

question.text: Pakistan came into being on
question.explanation: Pakistan's independence was celebrated on 14 August 1947, the day the transfer of power took effect for the new dominion.

question.text: Jinnah took the oath as the first Governor-General of Pakistan on
question.explanation: Jinnah was sworn in as Governor-General on 15 August 1947, the day after the independence celebrations.

question.text: Who was elected the first President of the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan?
question.explanation: Jinnah was elected President of the Constituent Assembly on 11 August 1947 and delivered his celebrated address on that occasion.

question.text: In his address to the Constituent Assembly on 11 August 1947 Jinnah stressed
options: freedom of religion for every citizen of the new state
the abolition of the princely states
the recovery of Kashmir by force
question.explanation: Jinnah told the Assembly that every citizen was free to go to his temple or mosque and that religion had nothing to do with the business of the state.

question.text: The Darul Uloom at Deoband was founded in 1866 by
question.explanation: Maulana Muhammad Qasim Nanautvi established the seminary at Deoband in 1866 to preserve traditional Islamic learning after 1857.

question.text: The Nadwatul Ulema was established in 1894 at
question.explanation: The Nadwatul Ulema was founded at Lucknow with the aim of combining religious learning with modern subjects.

question.text: The Anjuman-i-Himayat-i-Islam was founded in 1884 in which city?
question.explanation: The Anjuman-i-Himayat-i-Islam was set up at Lahore to promote education among Muslims and to counter missionary activity.

question.text: The Faraizi Movement in Bengal was founded by
question.explanation: Haji Shariatullah began the Faraizi Movement in Bengal to make Muslims observe the obligatory duties of Islam and to resist landlord oppression.

question.text: Syed Ahmad Barelvi was killed in 1831 in the battle of
question.explanation: Syed Ahmad Barelvi and Shah Ismail Shaheed fell at Balakot in 1831 fighting the Sikh forces.

question.text: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 with the help of
question.explanation: Allan Octavian Hume, a retired British civil servant, took the leading part in organising the Congress in 1885.

question.text: The Khudai Khidmatgar movement was founded by
question.explanation: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan organised the Khudai Khidmatgars, known as the Red Shirts, in the North-West Frontier Province and allied them with the Congress.

question.text: Who was the first Muslim to preside over a session of the Indian National Congress?
question.explanation: Badruddin Tyabji presided over the Congress session of 1887 at Madras, the first Muslim to hold that office.

question.text: The Khaksar Movement was founded by
question.explanation: Allama Inayatullah Khan Mashriqi founded the Khaksar Movement, whose members drilled with spades as a symbol of service and discipline.

question.text: The highest mountain peak of Pakistan is
question.explanation: K2, at 8,611 metres, is the highest peak in Pakistan and the second highest in the world after Mount Everest.

question.text: K2 is situated in which mountain range?
question.explanation: K2 stands in the Karakoram range on the Pakistan-China frontier in Gilgit-Baltistan.

question.text: Nanga Parbat lies in which mountain range?
question.explanation: Nanga Parbat, 8,126 metres high, is the western anchor of the Himalayan range and lies in Diamer district.

question.text: The highest peak of the Hindu Kush range is
question.explanation: Tirich Mir, 7,708 metres, in Chitral district is the highest peak of the Hindu Kush.

question.text: How many peaks above 8,000 metres are located in Pakistan?
question.explanation: Pakistan has five eight-thousanders: K2, Nanga Parbat, Gasherbrum I, Broad Peak and Gasherbrum II.

question.text: The Siachen Glacier lies in which mountain range?
question.explanation: Siachen is a long glacier of the eastern Karakoram range and is the world's highest battleground.

question.text: The Khunjerab Pass connects Pakistan with
question.explanation: The Khunjerab Pass in Gilgit-Baltistan is the border crossing between Pakistan and China's Xinjiang region.

question.text: The Khyber Pass links Pakistan with
question.explanation: The Khyber Pass runs from Peshawar valley through the Safed Koh to Afghanistan and has been the historic invasion route into the subcontinent.

question.text: The Shandur Pass connects Chitral with
question.explanation: Shandur, the site of the world's highest polo ground, links Chitral with Gilgit.

question.text: The Lowari Pass provides a route between Chitral and
question.explanation: The Lowari Pass, now bypassed by the Lowari Tunnel, connects Chitral with the Dir district.

question.text: The Babusar Pass links the Kaghan Valley with
question.explanation: Babusar Top joins the upper Kaghan Valley to Chilas on the Karakoram Highway.

question.text: The Indus River rises in
question.explanation: The Indus originates in the Tibetan plateau near Lake Mansarovar before entering Gilgit-Baltistan.

question.text: The Kabul River joins the Indus at
question.explanation: The Kabul River meets the Indus near Attock, just below Khairabad.

question.text: The Panjnad River joins the Indus near
question.explanation: The combined waters of the five eastern rivers form the Panjnad, which enters the Indus at Mithankot.

question.text: Tarbela Dam is built on which river?
question.explanation: Tarbela, in Swabi district, is an earth-filled dam on the Indus completed in 1976.

question.text: Mangla Dam is constructed on which river?
question.explanation: Mangla Dam, completed in 1967, impounds the Jhelum River near Mirpur in Azad Kashmir.

question.text: Warsak Dam has been built on which river?
question.explanation: Warsak Dam lies on the Kabul River about twenty kilometres from Peshawar.

question.text: The Diamer-Bhasha Dam is being constructed on which river?
question.explanation: Diamer-Bhasha is a concrete gravity dam on the Indus upstream of Tarbela.

question.text: The Mohmand Dam is being built on which river?
question.explanation: Mohmand Dam is a hydropower and storage project on the Swat River in Mohmand district.

question.text: The Sukkur Barrage on the Indus was completed in
question.explanation: Formerly called the Lloyd Barrage, Sukkur Barrage was completed in 1932 and feeds one of the world's largest irrigation systems.

question.text: The Ghulam Muhammad Barrage on the Indus is commonly known as
question.explanation: Kotri Barrage near Hyderabad is officially named the Ghulam Muhammad Barrage and is the lowest barrage on the Indus.

question.text: The largest desert of Pakistan is the
question.explanation: The Thar Desert of southeastern Sindh is the largest desert in Pakistan and extends into Indian Rajasthan.

question.text: The Thal Desert lies between the Indus and which other river?
question.explanation: Thal occupies the doab between the Indus and the Jhelum in districts such as Bhakkar and Layyah.

question.text: The largest freshwater lake of Pakistan is
question.explanation: Manchar Lake in Sindh, west of the Indus, is the largest natural freshwater lake in Pakistan.

question.text: Keenjhar Lake mainly supplies drinking water to which city?
question.explanation: Keenjhar (Kalri) Lake in Thatta district is the principal source of piped water for Karachi.

question.text: Lake Saiful Muluk is located in which valley?
question.explanation: Saiful Muluk is an alpine lake near Naran in the Kaghan Valley of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

question.text: Attabad Lake, formed by a landslide in 2010, lies in which valley?
question.explanation: A massive landslide at Attabad in January 2010 blocked the Hunza River and created the lake.

question.text: Hanna Lake is situated near which city?
question.explanation: Hanna Lake lies in the Urak valley a short distance from Quetta.

question.text: The largest province of Pakistan by area is
question.explanation: Balochistan covers about 347,190 square kilometres, roughly 44 per cent of Pakistan's territory.

question.text: The total area of Pakistan is approximately
question.explanation: Pakistan's area is officially given as 796,096 square kilometres.

question.text: The length of Pakistan's coastline is approximately
question.explanation: Pakistan's Arabian Sea coastline of about 1,046 kilometres is shared between Sindh and Balochistan.

question.text: Pakistan's shortest international land border is with
question.explanation: The Pakistan-China boundary along the Karakoram is the shortest of Pakistan's land borders.

question.text: The Durand Line between Pakistan and Afghanistan was demarcated in
question.explanation: The line was agreed in 1893 between Sir Mortimer Durand and Amir Abdur Rahman Khan of Afghanistan.

question.text: The Sir Creek dispute concerns the boundary between Sindh and the Indian state of
question.explanation: Sir Creek is a tidal estuary in the Rann of Kutch marking the disputed Sindh-Gujarat maritime boundary.

question.text: Gwadar was purchased by Pakistan in 1958 from
question.explanation: Gwadar had been an enclave of the Sultanate of Oman and was bought by Pakistan in 1958.

question.text: Port Qasim is located near which city?
question.explanation: Port Qasim, Pakistan's second busiest port, lies on the Indus delta creeks southeast of Karachi.

question.text: The Khewra Salt Mine is located in which district?
question.explanation: Khewra, in Jhelum district of Punjab, is one of the largest rock-salt mines in the world.

question.text: The Saindak copper and gold project is located in which district?
question.explanation: Saindak lies in Chagai district of Balochistan near the Iranian and Afghan borders.

question.text: The Sui gas field lies in which district of Balochistan?
question.explanation: Sui is located in Dera Bugti district in eastern Balochistan.

question.text: The Mari gas field is located in which province?
question.explanation: The Mari gas field lies near Daharki in the Ghotki area of upper Sindh.

question.text: The Thar coalfield is located in which province?
question.explanation: The Thar lignite deposits in Tharparkar district of Sindh are among the largest coal reserves in the world.

question.text: Muslim Bagh, known for chromite mining, is located in which province?
question.explanation: Muslim Bagh in Killa Saifullah district of Balochistan is Pakistan's main chromite producing area.

question.text: Emerald mines in Pakistan are chiefly located in which valley?
question.explanation: The emerald deposits near Mingora in the Swat valley are Pakistan's best known source of the gemstone.

question.text: Kalabagh, known for its iron ore deposits, lies in which district?
question.explanation: The Kalabagh iron ore field is in Mianwali district of Punjab on the right bank of the Indus.

question.text: The Deosai Plains are located in
question.explanation: Deosai, near Skardu in Gilgit-Baltistan, is one of the highest plateaus in the world and a national park.

question.text: The Salt Range lies between the Jhelum River and which other river?
question.explanation: The Salt Range stretches across northern Punjab between the Jhelum and the Indus, south of the Potohar Plateau.

question.text: The largest national park of Pakistan by area is
question.explanation: Hingol National Park on the Makran coast of Balochistan is the largest national park in Pakistan.

question.text: Astola Island, the largest island of Pakistan, lies off the coast of
question.explanation: Astola, also called Jezira Haft Talar, lies in the Arabian Sea off the Makran coast near Pasni.

question.text: The capital of Azad Jammu and Kashmir is
question.explanation: Muzaffarabad, on the confluence of the Neelum and Jhelum rivers, is the capital of Azad Jammu and Kashmir.

question.text: Changa Manga, one of the largest planted forests of Pakistan, is located in which province?
question.explanation: Changa Manga is a man-made irrigated plantation in Kasur district of Punjab.

question.text: The monsoon rains in Pakistan generally occur between
question.explanation: The summer monsoon reaches Pakistan in early July and withdraws by September, bringing most of the annual rainfall.

question.text: The largest food crop of Pakistan in terms of area sown is
question.explanation: Wheat, a Rabi crop, occupies the largest cultivated area and is the staple food grain of Pakistan.

question.text: The province producing the largest share of Pakistan's cotton is
question.explanation: Punjab's southern districts account for the greater part of national cotton output, with Sindh second.

question.text: Faisalabad is popularly known as
question.explanation: Faisalabad earned the title because of its concentration of cotton textile mills.

question.text: Sialkot is chiefly known for the manufacture of
question.explanation: Sialkot is the centre of Pakistan's sports goods, leather and surgical instrument industries.

question.text: Pakistan Steel Mills was set up with the technical and financial assistance of
question.explanation: The Karachi steel mill was built at Pipri under a 1971 agreement with the Soviet Union.

question.text: The Heavy Mechanical Complex of Pakistan is located at
question.explanation: The Heavy Mechanical Complex at Taxila, built with Chinese assistance, manufactures industrial plant and machinery.

question.text: Pakistan's first nuclear power plant, KANUPP, began operating in
question.explanation: The Karachi Nuclear Power Plant, built with Canadian assistance, was commissioned in 1972.

question.text: The State Bank of Pakistan was established on
question.explanation: The State Bank of Pakistan was inaugurated by Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah on 1 July 1948.

question.text: The fiscal year of the Government of Pakistan runs from
question.explanation: Pakistan's financial year begins on 1 July and closes on 30 June.

question.text: The largest single category of Pakistan's exports is
question.explanation: Textiles and made-up garments have long accounted for roughly three-fifths of Pakistan's export earnings.

question.text: The largest group of Pakistan's imports by value is
question.explanation: Petroleum crude and refined products form Pakistan's biggest import bill and drive its trade deficit.

question.text: The Economic Survey of Pakistan is published each year by the
question.explanation: The Ministry of Finance issues the Economic Survey a day before the federal budget is presented.

question.text: The Pakistan Stock Exchange was created in 2016 by merging the stock exchanges of
question.explanation: The Karachi, Lahore and Islamabad stock exchanges were integrated into the Pakistan Stock Exchange in January 2016.

question.text: The nationalization of major industries, banks and insurance companies in Pakistan was carried out under
question.explanation: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto's government began nationalizing basic industries in 1972 and banks in 1974.

question.text: The Green Revolution in Pakistan's agriculture took place mainly during the government of
question.explanation: High-yielding seed varieties, tubewells and fertilizer use spread rapidly in the 1960s under Ayub Khan.

question.text: Pakistan's First Five Year Plan covered the period
question.explanation: The First Five Year Plan ran from 1955 to 1960, though it was formally approved only in 1957.

question.text: The Motorway M-2 connects Islamabad with
question.explanation: The M-2, Pakistan's first motorway, links Islamabad with Lahore and was opened in 1997.

question.text: National Highway N-5, the Grand Trunk Road, runs from Karachi to
question.explanation: N-5 is Pakistan's longest national highway, running from Karachi through Lahore and Rawalpindi to Peshawar.

question.text: The China-Pakistan Economic Corridor links Gwadar with which Chinese city?
question.explanation: CPEC connects Gwadar port to Kashgar in China's Xinjiang region by road, rail and pipeline routes.

question.text: The main CPEC agreements were signed in April 2015 during the visit to Pakistan of
question.explanation: Chinese President Xi Jinping's April 2015 visit produced the package of CPEC agreements worth about 46 billion dollars.

question.text: The operational control of Gwadar Port was transferred in 2013 to a company of
question.explanation: Operations passed from the Port of Singapore Authority to the China Overseas Ports Holding Company in 2013.

question.text: The Indus Waters Treaty between Pakistan and India was signed in
question.explanation: The treaty was signed on 19 September 1960 after nine years of negotiation.

question.text: The Indus Waters Treaty was negotiated through the good offices of
question.explanation: The World Bank mediated the dispute and remains a signatory and guarantor of the treaty.

question.text: Under the Indus Waters Treaty the eastern rivers allotted to India are
question.explanation: India received unrestricted use of the Ravi, Beas and Sutlej, while Pakistan received the Indus, Jhelum and Chenab.

question.text: The Indus Waters Treaty was signed on behalf of Pakistan by
question.explanation: President Ayub Khan signed for Pakistan and Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru for India.

question.text: The Indus Waters Treaty was signed in which city?
question.explanation: The treaty was signed at Karachi, then the capital of Pakistan, in September 1960.

question.text: The body established under the Indus Waters Treaty to handle routine questions between the two countries is the
question.explanation: Each country appoints an Indus Commissioner, and together they form the Permanent Indus Commission.

question.text: The ceasefire ending the first Kashmir war between Pakistan and India came into effect on
question.explanation: A United Nations sponsored ceasefire took effect on 1 January 1949 and produced the ceasefire line in Kashmir.

question.text: The 1965 war between Pakistan and India on the international border began on
question.explanation: Indian forces crossed the international border towards Lahore on 6 September 1965, now observed as Defence Day.

question.text: The Pakistani operation launched in Kashmir in August 1965 was code-named
question.explanation: Operation Gibraltar sent infiltrators into Indian-held Kashmir and led to the escalation of the 1965 war.

question.text: The Tashkent Declaration ending the 1965 war was signed in
question.explanation: Ayub Khan and Lal Bahadur Shastri signed the declaration on 10 January 1966.

question.text: The Tashkent talks of 1966 were mediated by
question.explanation: Soviet Premier Alexei Kosygin hosted and mediated the talks at Tashkent in Soviet Uzbekistan.

question.text: Dhaka fell to Indian forces on
question.explanation: The Pakistani eastern command surrendered at Dhaka on 16 December 1971, ending the war in East Pakistan.

question.text: The Simla Agreement was signed by Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and
question.explanation: Indian Prime Minister Indira Gandhi signed the agreement with Pakistan's President Zulfikar Ali Bhutto.

question.text: Pakistan formally recognized Bangladesh in
question.explanation: Pakistan recognized Bangladesh in February 1974, shortly before the second Islamic Summit at Lahore.

question.text: The second Islamic Summit Conference was held in 1974 at
question.explanation: Lahore hosted the second summit of the Organisation of the Islamic Conference in February 1974.
